Designed specifically for vertical smartphone reading, every page is formatted to a 1092 × 1955 px (9:16 portrait) canvas using stacked panels, bold ink outlines, and vibrant space colors.   Completed Portrait Pages:Page 1 (Introduction): Introduces Kepi’s mission and explains the Transit Method and Light Curve graphs.   Page 5 (Interactive Activity Lab): Features a Light Curve guide, a mystery-planet matching game (ages 4–10), an orbit speed puzzle (ages 11–18), a printable Certified Exoplanet Explorer badge, and a NASA QR code.   Page 6 (The K2 Miracle): Chronicles the 2013 reaction-wheel breakdown and how NASA engineers balanced Kepi using sunlight pressure. Project Details: Kepi’s Exoplanet Adventure (Interactive Educational Comic)

1. What It Does & How It Works Kepi’s Exoplanet Adventure is a 9-page mobile-optimized educational comic series that teaches space science and exoplanet discovery through the eyes of Kepi, a cute chibi-style personification of NASA’s Kepler space telescope. Formatted in a vertical 1092 × 1955 px (9:16 portrait) layout with stacked panels, readers scroll through Kepi’s journey from its launch and Light Curve transit method, to surviving its 2013 reaction-wheel breakdown via the solar-powered K2 mission, and finally celebrating its scientific legacy alongside other retired space explorers. Beyond passive reading, the comic features an Interactive Activity Lab (Page 5) with tiered mini-games for different age groups, collector cards of real exoplanets (Kepler-16b, Kepler-186f, Kepler-10b, and K2-18b), a printable Certified Exoplanet Explorer badge, and a scannable QR code linking directly to NASA’s official exoplanet portal (exoplanets.nasa.gov).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Accessible STEM Education: Translates complex astrophysical concepts—such as transit photometry, orbital periods, Habitable ("Goldilocks") Zones, and photon pressure—into clear, visual storytelling.
  • Multi-Age Engagement: Differentiates activities so younger learners (ages 4–10) can match planet sizes to brightness dips, while older students (ages 11–18) analyze orbital timelines and exoplanet classification charts.
  • Inspiring Citizen Science: Encourages readers to continue exploring real astronomical data through NASA’s Planet Hunters TESS initiative and Kepi’s public archives.

3. Tools & Software Used

  • Generative AI Art & Prompt Engineering: Used to illustrate consistent chibi character designs, cosmic environments, and structured comic panels.
  • Canva (Graphic Design & Layout): Used to assemble the 1092 × 1955 px vertical canvases, refine typography and speech bubbles, remove backgrounds, and generate functional QR codes.

4. Creativity & Key Design Considerations

  • Creativity: Replaces dry textbook diagrams with an empathetic, expressive telescope hero, trading-card style planet profiles, and a "Silent Hall of Fame" framing retired spacecraft (Apollo 11, Opportunity, Voyager 1) as space heritage monuments rather than abandoned hardware.
    • Mobile-First Readability: Vertical 9:16 panel stacking ensures effortless reading on smartphones without zooming.
    • Scientific Accuracy: Every distance, orbital period, and mission milestone (2009 launch, 2013 K2 recovery, October 2018 retirement) is grounded in verified NASA mission data.
    • Visual Consistency: Maintained a cohesive dark-space palette, bold ink outlines, and uniform character proportions across all pages.
